beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A function is a rule that gives every input exactly one output.

do.meaning: A rule that gives every input exactly one output.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A vending machine is one. Press B four: chips. The button is the input; the snack is the output.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: C two gives chips too.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Two buttons give the same snack. I think that breaks the rule.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: No. Each button still gives just one snack.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So B four giving chips or nuts would break it: one input, two different outputs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: An ordered pair puts the input first, the output second. Negative two, one means negative two gives one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A relation is a set of these pairs. Add one, three: one gives three.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three, one will work too. Two inputs share one output, like the buttons.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: List one, three again. It lands on the same arrow; no new output.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: But one, negative two adds a second output for one. Not a function.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The pairs are also points. Input x measures across; output y measures up or down. One, three is right one, up three.

do.text: Input: across. Output: up or down.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One, negative two sits directly below it. Same input, different outputs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A vertical line checks one input. Sweep across: two points at one means not a function. A function has at most one point per vertical line. No points means that input is unused.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To make this a function, which single point could we remove?

do.text: To make this a function, which single point could we remove?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Either B or C. Remove B: one output remains. Or put B back and remove C. Removing another point leaves both conflicting points.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try adding four, three. Four is a new input, so it works, even though the output three is shared.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: But adding one, negative two fails. One already gives three. Same input, different height.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Add k, four to our pairs: since none of their outputs is four, k must avoid the used inputs, negative two, one, and three.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: A new input, like four, works; a used input would get two different outputs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which list represents a function?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: B. The repeated pair adds nothing. Negative two and three each give one. A fails: negative two gives both one and three.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Follow each input. Exactly one arrow leaves it. One input, one output.
